ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the function $y=kx+b$ ($k\neq 0$) passes through point $B(2,0)$ and intersects with the graph of the function $y=2x$ at point $A$. Then, what is the solution set of the inequality $0<kx+b<2x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $y=2$, solving $2=2x$ gives $x=1$, \\
$\therefore$ point A is (1, 2), \\
$\therefore$ for $x>1$, $2x>kx+b$, \\
$\because$ the graph of the function $y=kx+b$ ($k \ne 0$) passes through point B (2, 0), \\
$\therefore$ for $x<2$, $kx+b>0$, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set for the inequality $0<kx+b<2x$ is $1<x<2$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{1<x<2}$.
